subtitle: How Silver Bound a River Kingdom Together

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle close-up of a silver tanka held between finger and thumb against the hazy outline of Bengal’s rivers and ports
panels.action: The Bengal Sultanate Tanka Master stands in shadow, holding up a gleaming silver tanka stamped with mint and sultan’s titles, the Bengal delta’s tangled rivers and distant ships faintly visible behind him.

dialogue.text: From Pandua to Chittagong, twenty-seven-plus mints struck silver tankas—each coin a tiny decree: the Sultans of Bengal exist, and their name must pass through every hand.

i18n.hi: पांडुआ से चिटगाँव तक, सत्ताईस से ज़्यादा टकसालों ने चाँदी के टंका ढाले—हर सिक्का एक छोटा हुक्म: बंगाल के सुल्तान हैं, और उनका नाम हर हाथ से गुज़रेगा।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a tabletop scattered with silver tankas from different mints, each partially visible with varying inscriptions
panels.action: The Bengal Sultanate Tanka Master leans over a wooden table where neat piles of silver tankas lie, each with different mint names and dates, a dim oil lamp throwing sharp light over their surfaces.

dialogue.text: The chronicles speak of kings and battles. The coins of Bengal speak of something else: cities, ports, titles and years punched into silver from at least twenty-seven mints.

i18n.hi: इतिहास में बादशाहों और जंगों की बातें हैं। बंगाल के सिक्के और कुछ कहते हैं: शहर, बंदरगाह, किताबें और साल, कम से कम सत्ताईस टकसालों से चाँदी पर ठोंके गए।

panels.shot: wide aerial view of the Bengal delta, braided rivers glinting, dots of towns and ports along the waterways
panels.action: A sweeping vista shows the Bengal delta in the 14th–16th centuries, broad rivers curling through green plains, clusters of wooden houses and mosque domes at Pandua, Gaur, Sonargaon and distant river ports.

dialogue.text: Here, in the flooded world of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta, power could not cling to one hilltop. It had to float, to travel, to reach every river bend where merchants counted their gains.

i18n.hi: गंगा-ब्रह्मपुत्र डेल्टा की डूबती दुनिया में ताकत एक टीले पर नहीं टिकती। उसे तैरना होता है, चलना होता है, हर मोड़ तक पहुँचना होता है जहाँ सौदागर हिसाब गिनते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a bustling Sonargaon bazaar, with stalls, weavers, and traders exchanging coins by hand
panels.action: In Sonargaon’s crowded bazaar, cloth merchants, rice sellers and sailors haggle, their hands flicking small silver disks from palm to palm as scales hang and boats wait at the riverside.

dialogue.text: By the time Ibn Battuta reached Bengal around 1338, silver tankas already rang through market stalls. His travelogue hints at a moneyed land, where coins smoothed trade across water and mud.

i18n.hi: जब इब्न बतूता तेरह सौ अड़तीस के आस-पास बंगाल पहुँचे, चाँदी के टंका बाज़ारों में झनक रहे थे। उनकी सफ़रनामा एक दौलतमंद ज़मीन का इशारा देता है, जहाँ सिक्के पानी और कीचड़ पर सौदा आसान करते थे।

panels.shot: close-up of a single tanka being examined under lamplight, inscriptions just legible: sultan’s name, mint, AH date
panels.action: The Bengal Sultanate Tanka Master holds a tanka close to the lamp, its Arabic script clearly showing the sultan’s laqab, the mint name ‘Firuzabad’ or ‘Lakhnauti,’ and a Hijri date in fine calligraphy.

dialogue.speaker: the_sultans_of_bengal
dialogue.text: Name, title, city, year—this is how a realm speaks without raising its voice.

i18n.hi: नाम, ख़िताब, शहर, साल—यही है कि सल्तनत बिना चीखे कैसे बोलती है।

panels.shot: diagrammatic-style wide shot of Bengal with lines radiating from multiple key mints to hinterland markets
panels.action: A map-like scene shows Gaur/Lakhnauti, Pandua, Sonargaon, Satgaon, Chittagong and Khalifatabad marked as bright hubs, thin glowing lines reaching from them to clusters of village fairs and river piers.

dialogue.text: Numismatists like Nicholas Rhodes read these inscriptions as a network. Gaur, Pandua, Sonargaon, Satgaon, Chittagong, Khalifatabad—each mint tied its region’s trade to the sultan’s silver promise.

i18n.hi: निकोलस रोड्स जैसे सिक्का-विद इन लिखावटों को जाल जैसा पढ़ते हैं। गौर, पांडुआ, सोनारगाँव, सातगाँव, चिटगाँव, ख़लिफ़ताबाद—हर टकसाल अपने इलाक़े के सौदे को सुल्तान की चाँदी की ज़मानत से बाँधता है।

panels.shot: interior of a mint at Pandua, busy but orderly, with furnaces, dies, and workers striking coins on anvils
panels.action: Inside a Pandua mint, workers sit cross-legged, heating silver blanks and placing them on iron dies, another man raising a hammer, frozen mid-strike as rows of finished tankas gleam in wooden trays.

dialogue.text: A mint was part workshop, part chancery. Here, scribes chose titles, die-cutters carved letters, and hammer-men beat the royal message into metal, hundreds of times a day.

i18n.hi: टकसाल आधी कार्यशाला, आधी दफ़्तर थी। यहाँ क़लमची ख़िताब चुनते, नक्काश अक्षर काटते, और हथौड़े वाले रोज़ सैकड़ों बार बादशाह का पैग़ाम धातु में ठोकते।

panels.shot: close-up montage of different tankas showing varying titulature, some emphasizing piety, others conquest
panels.action: A tight montage shows multiple tankas: one with a pious title, another with a long string of victorious epithets, yet another with the mint name of Chittagong, each coin’s edge catching the light.

dialogue.text: Titles shifted with politics. Some issues praised God and justice; others boasted of conquests. Husain Shah’s coins trumpet victories, yet their silver still had to be trusted in the smallest village stall.

i18n.hi: सियासत के साथ ख़िताब बदलते रहे। कुछ सिक्के ख़ुदा और इंसाफ की बातें करते, कुछ फ़तहें जताते। हुसैन शाह के सिक्के जीतें पुकारते हैं, पर उनकी चाँदी को सबसे छोटे देहाती ठेले पर भी यक़ीन की ज़रूरत थी।

panels.shot: port wide shot at Satgaon, ships from inland rivers and sea converging, sailors and brokers trading bales and coins
panels.action: At Satgaon’s riverside port, ocean-going ships sit alongside river boats as sailors unload cotton and spices, brokers squat with heaps of goods while hands flash silver tankas between them in quick deals.

dialogue.text: Satgaon and Sonargaon fed the sea routes. A merchant stepping off his ship needed one thing: a coin whose weight and inscription he could trust. Bengal’s silver tankas made inland produce speak a global language.

i18n.hi: सातगाँव और सोनारगाँव समुद्री रस्तों को खिलाते थे। जहाज़ से उतरते व्यापारी को बस एक चीज़ चाहिए थी: ऐसा सिक्का जिसका वज़न और लिखावट भरोसेमंद हो। बंगाल के चाँदी टंका ने अंदरूनी माल को दुनिया की भाषा दे दी।

panels.shot: medium shot of a rural market deep in the delta, a local elder weighing a tanka on a small scale
panels.action: In a muddy village haat far from any capital, an elderly trader in simple clothes carefully places a tanka on a tiny balance scale, squinting at its swing before nodding to a farmer with sacks of rice.

dialogue.text: The innovation lay in reach. Decentralized mints meant that even a flooded backwater could see fresh royal coin. Money knit places together that the court’s cavalry could never visit in a year.

i18n.hi: असली नयी बात पहुँच में थी। बिखरी हुई टकसालों का मतलब था कि डूबा हुआ पिछड़ा इलाक़ा भी ताज़ा शाही सिक्का देख सकता था। पैसा उन जगहों को जोड़ता रहा जहाँ दरबार की फ़ौज साल भर में भी नहीं पहुँच पाती।

panels.shot: medium shot of the Tanka Master comparing two coins, one from Gaur and one from Chittagong, thoughtful expression
panels.action: The Bengal Sultanate Tanka Master sits cross-legged, a Gaur tanka in one hand and a Chittagong tanka in the other, eyes narrowed as he compares their calligraphy and imagines their journeys.

dialogue.text: For historians today, these coins correct the written record. Hijri dates and mint names can be firmer than later chronicles, which remember stories but blur years and distances.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकारों के लिए ये सिक्के लिखे रिकॉर्ड को दुरुस्त करते हैं। हिजरी तारीखें और टकसाल के नाम अक्सर बाद की किताबों से ज़्यादा ठोस होते हैं, जो किस्से तो याद रखती हैं पर साल और दूरियाँ धुंधला देती हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the Tanka Master pointing to a coin inscription that lists a distant region among the sultan’s titles
panels.action: The Bengal Sultanate Tanka Master’s finger rests on a coin whose inscription lists a distant region as part of the sultan’s style, the letters sharp and proud against the smooth silver.

dialogue.text: Yet coin boasts have limits. A tanka may claim a province in its royal style, but without other evidence, scholars hesitate to treat every word as proof of permanent control on the ground.

i18n.hi: पर सिक्कों की शान की भी हद होती है। एक टंका अपने ख़िताब में किसी सूबे पर दावा कर सकता है, मगर बिना दूसरे सबूत के, विद्वान ज़मीन पर हमेशा की पकड़ मानने से हिचकते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Chittagong harbor with ships leaving, a money-changer’s table in foreground stacked with different regional coins
panels.action: At Chittagong’s busy harbor, a money-changer sits beside coiled ropes and cargo, small heaps of foreign coins on one side and neat stacks of Bengal silver tankas on the other as ships prepare to sail.

dialogue.text: Chittagong’s mints supplied this frontier to the ocean. Here, Bengal’s money met coins from elsewhere, converted, measured, judged—its reputation tested with every exchange across the water.

i18n.hi: चिटगाँव की टकसालों ने इस सरहद को समंदर तक रसद दी। यहाँ बंगाल का पैसा दूसरे इलाकों के सिक्कों से मिला, बदला गया, तौला गया, परखा गया—हर पार के सौदे पर उसकी शोहरत की जाँच हुई।

panels.shot: interior of Khalifatabad mint, more modest, with a qadi overseeing, hinting at local religious authority tied to coinage
panels.action: Inside a smaller Khalifatabad mint, a local qadi watches workers weighing silver blanks on a simple scale while a clerk records numbers, the modest furnace glowing in the corner.

dialogue.text: Mints also carried faith and law. In places like Khalifatabad, the coinage linked local judges and mosque communities to the distant sultan. The tanka became proof that his authority reached their streets.

i18n.hi: टकसालें ईमान और क़ानून भी ढोती थीं। ख़लिफ़ताबाद जैसे इलाक़ों में सिक्का स्थानीय क़ाज़ियों और मस्जिद के लोगों को दूर बैठे सुल्तान से जोड़ता था। टंका सबूत बन जाता था कि उसका हुक्म उनकी गलियों तक पहुँचता है।

panels.shot: low-angle shot in a royal audience hall, Tanka Master presenting new coin designs to a silhouetted sultan on the throne
panels.action: In a lofty audience hall, the Bengal Sultanate Tanka Master kneels, presenting trays of newly struck tankas to a shadowed sultan on the throne, courtiers watching as if the coins were decrees made metal.

dialogue.speaker: the_sultans_of_bengal
dialogue.text: Your reign will be read not only in ink, Majesty, but in silver.

i18n.hi: आपका दौर सिर्फ़ स्याही में नहीं पढ़ा जाएगा, जहांपनाह, चाँदी में भी।

panels.shot: montage showing coins traveling: in a merchant’s pouch on a boat, in a tax collector’s chest, buried in a hoard underground
panels.action: A three-part scene shows a leather pouch of tankas tied at a boatman’s waist, a heavy tax chest being carried into a treasury, and a secret hoard of coins half-buried in damp earth beneath a house.

dialogue.text: Over decades, silver flowed out as pay and tax, and back again as hoards and revenue. Long after a sultan died, his name still rested in soil and chests, stamped on coins that refused to vanish.

i18n.hi: बरसों तक चाँदी मज़दूरी और लगान बनकर बाहर निकली, और ख़ज़ाने व माल-ए-मुक़र्रर बनकर वापस आई। सुल्तान के मरने के बहुत बाद भी उसका नाम मिट्टी और संदूकों में पड़ा रहता, उन सिक्कों पर जो मिटने से इनकार करते।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot of the capital shifting from Pandua to Gaur, coins from both mints shown overlapping in foreground
panels.action: A blended view shows old Pandua’s mosques fading as Gaur’s city walls brighten, while in the foreground tankas from both ‘Firuzabad’ and ‘Lakhnauti’ lie side by side, equally bright under the same light.

dialogue.text: Capitals moved—from Pandua to Gaur—but the coin system endured. Mints rose and fell, yet the habit remained: to make power tangible as weight and purity that could survive political turns.

i18n.hi: राजधानियाँ बदलीं—पांडुआ से गौर तक—पर सिक्का तंत्र चला रहा। टकसालें उठीं, गिरीं, पर आदत क़ायम रही: ताकत को वज़न और ख़ालिसियत में बदलना जो सियासी पलटनों के बाद भी बची रह सके।

panels.shot: modern-style excavation scene, archaeologists dusting off a hoard of Bengal tankas in a trench
panels.action: In a present-day dig, archaeologists crouch in a trench, gently brushing soil from a clustered hoard of Bengal silver tankas, their designs reappearing after centuries in the dark.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, buried hoards and museum trays let scholars reconstruct this monetary architecture. The coins speak calmly, showing dates, mints and shifts in style that chronicles barely remember.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, गड़े ख़ज़ाने और अजीब-अजीब संग्रहों की तश्तरियाँ विद्वानों को इस नक़दी के ढाँचे को फिर जोड़ने देती हैं। सिक्के ठंडे अंदाज़ में बोलते हैं, तारीखें, टकसालें और अंदाज के बदलाव दिखाते हैं जिन्हें किताबें मुश्किल से याद रखती हैं।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of the Tanka Master’s hand releasing a tanka into another outstretched palm, background fading to abstract river patterns
panels.action: The Bengal Sultanate Tanka Master opens his hand to drop a single tanka into another person’s waiting palm, while behind them the scene blurs into flowing river lines and faint city silhouettes.

dialogue.text: In the end, a state in Bengal became real not through fort walls alone, but when its silver was trusted. Each tanka closed a deal, settled a tax, and quietly affirmed that the sultan’s word still held.

i18n.hi: आखिर में, बंगाल की सल्तनत सिर्फ़ क़िले की दीवारों से नहीं, तब हक़ीक़ी बनी जब उसकी चाँदी पर यक़ीन हुआ। हर टंका सौदा पक्का करता, लगान चुकाता, और चुपचाप ये यक़ीन दिलाता कि सुल्तान का शब्द अभी भी चलता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: How Silver Bound a River Kingdom Together
subtitle_i18n.hi: चाँदी ने कैसे नदी के राज्य को जोड़ा
